_doc: THE ONE PIN of the gh binary libs:gh ships (#646). build.gradle reads this file, downloads each ABI's official release tarball ONCE into build/, refuses on a sha256 mismatch of the tarball AND of the extracted binary (the #288 / #348 fetch-once-refuse-on-mismatch pattern, as libs:rclone does it), reads the ELF program headers and refuses if PT_INTERP is present, and lands the binary as jniLibs/<abi>/libgh.so. That name is not decoration: on API 29+ an app may not exec a file it wrote into its own data directory (W^X), but it MAY exec what the installer extracted into nativeLibraryDir, and only files named lib*.so get extracted there — which is also why the PACKAGING app must set packaging.jniLibs.useLegacyPackaging = true (AGP's default keeps .so files compressed inside the APK and mmaps them, extracting nothing). GhRunner execs applicationInfo.nativeLibraryDir + '/libgh.so'. #653 THE DEVICE-FLOW FIELDS ARE DELETED (device_code_url, token_url, verification_uri, client_ids) along with GhDeviceLogin.kt: this module no longer MINTS a GitHub credential. Sign-in is an ordinary Authelia browser login (auth.sign_in provider authelia_web) and the GitHub work happens SERVER-SIDE in git-proxy-api, so the phone never obtains a GitHub credential by typing a code at a URL. What is left is the binary and its hashes: gh USES a credential the vault import already delivered, and that is the whole of its fallback role. A baked device_code_url with no caller is a second source of truth waiting to grow one back, so it is deleted rather than left behind a flag. #689 SUPERSEDES THE SIGN-IN HALF OF THIS: the GitHub leg of Sync > Git now signs in with gh's OWN `auth login` (see _doc_login_output) and lists and clones through gh. Still nothing of the fleet's own is declared for it: no device_code_url, no client id, no secret, no redirect; gh carries its own client id.
_doc_interp: WHY THE OFFICIAL linux_{arch} BUILD RUNS ON ANDROID. gh's release binaries for linux_arm64 and linux_amd64 are Go builds with cgo disabled: measured 2026-09-29 on the real device (a0_docs/eng-specs/terminal-per-tool-libs-measurement.md §7b) and RE-MEASURED 2026-09-29 for this pin with an independent program-header walk over both binaries — NO PT_INTERP and NO PT_DYNAMIC, i.e. fully static, raw syscalls, no libc at all. Bionic vs glibc is therefore moot: nothing is dynamically linked, so the kernel runs it directly. That is the property `interp: none` below declares and build.gradle re-measures on every build; a future release that links dynamically fails the build here rather than dying ENOENT on a phone. DO NOT SUBSTITUTE THE NIXPKGS gh: the gh in this phone's nix store is a DIFFERENT artifact, 49,750,856 bytes with BOTH PT_INTERP and PT_DYNAMIC present, and it would be refused by the guard below. The official cli/cli release is the one pinned here; do not generalise from a distro build.
_doc_x86_64_16k: #1881 The x86_64 binary is NOT the upstream release: that one is linked with 4 KB pages and fails the 16 KB page-size policy. It is built from the upstream source tag source_tag (commit source_commit) by .github/workflows/build-engines-16k.yml (CGO off, static, go linker -R=16384, every PT_LOAD p_align 0x4000 checked in that job) and published as an asset of the immutable release engines-16k-r1; url and entry override the url_template and entry_template for this ABI. arm64 stays the upstream release.
_doc_size: 37.1 MB (arm64) / 40.0 MB (amd64) uncompressed — CHEAPER than the 78 MB rclone binary this shelf already ships. ~13-15 MB in the APK (the release tarball's own compression is the floor) and extracted once at install. A per-ABI split APK carries one of them.
_doc_selfcontained: ZERO CHILD EXECS, NO git, NO PATH, NO WRITABLE $HOME — all measured, including a real authenticated API round-trip (`gh api /user`) whose strace showed only gh's own execve and nothing else. gh shells out to git only for git-shaped subcommands, which the auth and REST paths this library uses never reach. GH_CONFIG_DIR overrides config AND state location completely, so the consuming app points it at its own filesDir and gh needs nothing from $HOME. That is what makes gh safe to exec from nativeLibraryDir in an Android sandbox.
_doc_login_output: #689 HOW THIS VERSION SPEAKS DURING `gh auth login` WITH NO TTY, which is how GhRunner runs it. MEASURED 2026-09-30 on this pin (aarch64, stdin /dev/null, GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1, --hostname github.com --git-protocol https --web --insecure-storage --skip-ssh-key --clipboard=false): a blank line, `! First copy your one-time code: B1D3-EA43`, `Open this URL to continue in your web browser: https://github.com/login/device`, then silence while gh polls until the code is approved or expires. That is gh's OWN device flow against the client id GitHub CLI compiles into this binary, so the fleet supplies no client id, no secret and no redirect. GhOutput reads the code and the URL with the two patterns below and nothing else; they are data because they are a property of THIS version, so a pin bump re-measures them here, beside the hashes they belong to. No backslash and no double quote in either: build.gradle bakes them as plain string literals. ac_cloud-drive/test/test-drive-git-gh-leg.sh executes both against the measured transcript. The #653 deletions stand: nothing here is a device_code_url or a client id of the fleet's own; gh carries its own.
_doc_sandbox: WHAT THE APP SANDBOX DOES NOT GIVE gh, read off gh 2.101.0's own sources (Go 1.27) after the phone showed 'check your internet connection or https://githubstatus.com' on Sync > Git while the same binary signed in fine outside the app. That sentence is gh's printError branch for a *net.DNSError and nothing else (internal/ghcmd/cmd.go): gh's sign-in never got as far as GitHub. The official linux build has cgo off, so Go's own resolver reads /etc/resolv.conf, which an Android app does not have; it then asks 127.0.0.1:53 and [::1]:53 (net/dnsconfig.go defaultNS), where nothing answers. Every earlier measurement in _doc_selfcontained ran inside com.termux.nix, whose rootfs HAS /etc/resolv.conf and /etc/ssl, which is why none of them saw it. The second gap waits right behind the first: crypto/x509 only adds Android's CA directory when GOOS=android (root_linux.go), so a linux build in an app finds no roots and every TLS handshake to GitHub would fail as an unknown authority. The fix is two facts the engine hands gh, both declared here. ssl_cert_dirs (libs/sysdns/data/sysdns.json since #741) becomes SSL_CERT_DIR, which Go reads on linux in place of its defaults (crypto/x509/root.go, ':'-separated; a missing directory is skipped). proxy_hosts is what ResolverProxy (libs:sysdns since #741, shared with every bundled binary), a loopback CONNECT proxy in the engine's own process, will open a tunnel to: gh gets HTTPS_PROXY pointing at it, Go dials the proxy by IP (no lookup), and the proxy resolves the name with Android's resolver. TLS stays end to end between gh and GitHub; the proxy sees only the host name. It is not an open relay: any other host or port is refused with a 403 that names the host, and every request must carry the per-process credential that only the engine's gh children are given. gh 2.101.0 talks to github.com for the device code and token and api.github.com for everything else; a host gh starts using later shows up as a refused CONNECT naming it, in logcat and in gh's own error line.

sandbox._doc_idle_close_ms: WHY A QUIET TUNNEL IS CLOSED. gh's device flow sends its token poll every 6s at the earliest (cli/oauth v1.2.2 device.Wait: the 5s interval GitHub gives, times its 1.2 safety margin) and Go reuses one kept-alive connection for every poll. On a phone the upstream half of that connection can die while it sits idle (a NAT64 mapping dropped on an IPv6-only network, sockets Android destroys while the engine is frozen or loses its network); the proxy only noticed when the next poll's bytes hit the dead socket, and gh, having already written its POST, got 'unexpected EOF' and gave up (Go never retries a POST that was written: net/http shouldRetryRequest). So once GitHub has answered and nothing moves either way for this long, GhNetProxy ends the tunnel cleanly: Go sees its idle connection close, drops it, and the next poll dials a fresh tunnel. A request still waiting for its answer (gh spoke last) is never cut. Must stay well below the 6s poll so the close lands before the poll, not under it.
